subject: Operator escrow / EU-only processing — evidentiary checklist + SCCs follow-up
messages:

To: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@medigen.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Nov 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: EU-only processing — operator escrow evidence request

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and legal teams are tightening the controls for EU-only processing. Two asks up front from Legal: 1) a clear list of evidence artifacts Redwood can provide to show that inference and logs remain in-region (including backups), and 2) details on operator/escrow access — what keys or processes would permit a remote operator to access data and how that is logged.

We have a Schrems II assessment in parallel and will need to map the SCCs clauses to your operator access controls (especially Sections 4–7). Can you share an evidence checklist and a sample operator-escrow process diagram?

Attachments from our side: a short questionnaire (attached) and our compliance contact Pierre (p.laurent@medigen.com).

Sofia Atkinson
Head of IT Risk, Medigen Health
sofia@medigen.com

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
To: Sofia Atkinson <sofia@medigen.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 21 Nov 2028 13:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU-only processing — operator escrow evidence request

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Lauren (privacy lead) and Naomi (ops/evidence) to provide the checklist and process artifact.

High level answers while they assemble the docs:
- We support EU-only processing via region pinning and in-region control-plane options; inference and short-lived KV caches are kept on EU-hosted compute by default for pinned deployments.
- Backups: encrypted backups are retained per customer retention policy and can be scoped to EU storage buckets; we have a documented retention & purge pipeline.
- Operator/escrow access: remote operator access requires multi-party authorization, and any key material used for emergency operator actions is placed in an HSM-backed escrow with recorded RBAC approvals and time-limited access tokens. Full logs are retained and made available for audits.

We will attach the evidence checklist, a diagram of the escrow flow, and a mapping of SCC clauses to controls. Expect the package from Naomi by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.example.com

Subject: Operator escrow & evidence pack (draft)

Hi Sofia — attached is a first-pass evidence bundle. Highlights below and quick notes on what we can provide vs. what requires on-site validation or a managed attestation: 

Attachments: sccs-mapping.xlsx (control mapping), operator-escrow-process.pdf (diagram + steps), evidence-checklist.csv (artifact inventory)

1) Evidence we can deliver electronically:
   - Region pinning config snapshot (export)
   - Backup manifest + retention policy docs
   - Audit trail extract for operator session logs (samples)
   - KMS/HSM custody statements and rotation logs

2) Evidence that typically requires customer-side sign-off or a joint audit:
   - On-premises operator access review (if customer requests a physical witness)
   - End-to-end deletion verification for deeply archived backups (we can provide manifests and purge job records)

3) SCCs mapping notes:
   - We mapped relevant SCC clauses (4–7, 13–15) to our controls in the workbook. For claims around law enforcement access, we provide our process and DFIR escalation playbook.

Questions for you:
- Do you need redacted or fully detailed audit extracts?
- Any preferred format for the legal team (Excel, annotated PDF, or a formal attestation letter)?

I can produce a formal attestation draft and a sample DocuSign workflow if you want a sign-off artifact.

—Naomi
Senior Manager, Evidence & Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com
To: Pierre Laurent <p.laurent@medigen.com>, naomi_feldman@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: Mon, 27 Nov 2028 15:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Operator escrow & evidence pack (draft)

Hi Pierre — quick answers inline to your numbered items.

1) Sample operator session log: attached sample includes RBAC approval IDs, timestamped justifications, and session duration. We have redacted sensitive identifiers; full extracts can be provided under NDA or during a joint audit.

2) Escrow key lifecycle: keys that support emergency operator access are escrowed using a 3-of-5 split managed between Redwood HSM, our EMEA legal escrow partner (Kestrel Custody), and a locked recovery component held by a designated customer keyholder if requested. Release requires automated M-of-N approval plus a legal authorization token issued by our compliance team. We will provide the escrow agreement template and a controlled-keyflow diagram (attachment).

3) Restore jobs: by default, test restores are executed within EU regions. We run a small number of cross-region staging restores only in scheduled disaster-recovery drills (explicitly communicated, with customer opt-in). For pinned EU-only customers, we can guarantee no cross-region restore without prior written approval.

Next steps: Naomi will produce the Excel SCCs mapping and a one-page attestation draft for your counsel. If that works, we can schedule a 30-minute call mid-week to finalize language.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference
